Asma ties the Prophet's emigration food with her belt; sacrificial meat and Sawiq serve as journey food, the Prophet blesses dwindling provisions, and a huge fish feeds 300 men.
At Khaibar a man grabs a thrown container of fat, booty honey and grapes are eaten not stored, and the Prophet has pots of donkey meat overturned.
Feed the hungry, visit the sick and free captives; Muhammad's family never ate their fill three days running, and the Prophet fed a starving Abu Huraira milk until full.
The Prophet told his stepson Umar bin Abi Salama to say Allah's name, eat with his right hand and from what is nearest; he liked starting from the right.
The Prophet's household lived on dates and water, near Khaibar only sawiq; he ate no thin bread and not at tables but on leather sheets, as at Safiyya's wedding.
Mastigure meat, not unlawful, was eaten on the Prophet's dining sheet though he disliked it, not being of his people's land; at As-Sahba they ate only sawiq.
Food for two suffices three and for three suffices four; a believer eats in one intestine and a disbeliever in seven; a man ate less after embracing Islam.
The Prophet did not eat while leaning, and withdrew his hand from roasted mastigure, not unlawful but not found in his people's land, while Khalid ate it.
The Prophet drank milk and ate iqt but left the mastigures set on his dining sheet; Sahl's companions relished an old woman's silq and barley dish after Friday prayer.
The Prophet bit meat off a shoulder, stripped the foreleg of Abu Qatada's onager though in Ihram, and cut mutton with a knife, praying afterwards without renewing ablution.
The Prophet never criticised food; they had no white flour or sieves and ate unsifted barley, dates or leaves; his family never ate wheat bread their fill three days running.
The Prophet picked gourd from a tailor's tharid, never saw thin bread or a roasted sheep, Anas said, and cut mutton with a knife, praying without new ablution.
Hudhaifa threw back the cup a Magian brought him, citing the Prophet's ban on silk and on eating or drinking from gold or silver vessels, the unbelievers' in this world.
The Prophet loved sweets and honey; hungry Abu Huraira sought meals and praised Ja'far's kindness to the poor; the Prophet ate gourd at his slave tailor's house.
The Prophet picked gourd from a tailor's soup; Aisha said sacrifice meat was kept fifteen days; the family never ate wheat bread with meat their fill three days running.
The Prophet ate fresh dates with cucumber; Abu Huraira's share of dates from him included a hard, unripe one; and when he died, dates and water had sufficed them.
The date palm is like a Muslim; seven morning Ajwa dates guard against poison and magic; never two dates at once without leave; the Prophet ate them with cucumber.
After eating, the Prophet rinsed his mouth and prayed without new ablution; lick fingers before wiping them; he praised Allah after meals; a servant who cooked should get a share.
Abu Musa saw the Prophet eating chicken.
Abu Usaid's bride soaked dates overnight for the Prophet's drink; he forbade certain drink containers, such as Ad-Dubba', Al-Muzaffat and green jars, then allowed some to those in need.
The Prophet chose milk on his ascent, drank it at Arafat and from Abu Bakr on leaving Mecca, said to cover it, rinsed after it, and praised lending milch animals.
The Prophet drank milk mixed with water and passed it to his right, even a boy before elders; he liked sweets and honey, and he and Ali drank water standing.
At night cover vessels, tie water-skins and shut doors naming Allah; do not drink from a water-skin's mouth or breathe into the vessel, and the Prophet took three breaths drinking.
Gold and silver vessels, like silk, are for unbelievers here, and drinking in silver fills the belly with Hell Fire; Sahl and Anas kept bowls the Prophet drank from.
A bride served the Prophet soaked dates; Sauda soaked dates in a skin till worn out; his family never had their fill of wheat bread with meat three days running.
Mastigures were eaten on the Prophet's table cloth though he disliked them, so they were not unlawful; whoever eats garlic or onion should keep away from the mosque.
